tools.description: For Notion introductions, summaries, comparisons or inspection, copy a supplied Skill/resource ref into path. This reads content without loading Requires or activating its workflow. If the task already calls for applying a chosen Skill, call notion_use directly; it loads the root and Requires without a preliminary main read. For a requested latest-version inspection, use refresh:true with the supplied main Skill ref; the current task keeps its previous selection. To adopt the latest instructions, call notion_use with refresh:true directly. Reuse a complete successful read. Notion reads do not write to the remote library. Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete. Alternatively, paths reads fixed resources of one owner and snapshot together; choose path or paths. Batch reads exclude offset/limit and the main entrypoint.

budget.description: For a user-requested bounded wait on a resource paths batch only. timeBudgetMs covers the complete operation, including lookup and acquisition; default 30000, maximum 120000. File and byte limits stay unchanged. No automatic retry.

from.description: For an authored relative file link, copy the fixed sr:S/sr:R or canonical skill:// ref of the actual file containing that link. Put the original relative link or skill:// reference in path; an omitted Library binds from the containing file. Nested documents use their own resource ref, not the main Skill ref. Source-backed cross-Skill links resolve through the shared Source mapping; targets keep their own versions. Excludes paths batches and refresh:true.

path.description: Local file path (relative or absolute), an issued skill:// or sr: ref, or a supplied Notion Skill page URL. Notion main reads inspect without adopting task instructions. Copy refs verbatim; never guess filesystem paths.

paths.description: Copy complete resource refs verbatim from the selected Skill snapshot's resource directory. Every ref must identify a file in the same owner and snapshot. Reads all selected files in one operation without preparing the main body.

refresh.description: Use only for a user-requested current-version inspection; a successful complete read needs no follow-up refresh. Keeps the active selection unchanged. Only for a supplied Notion Skill ref in path; fixed resources and local files keep their versions.

tools.description: Search the authorized Skill metadata directory, including items outside the default View. Returns Skill refs for read or notion_use; it does not load instructions or activate workflows. For named Notion Skill existence or availability questions, set query to the name and refresh:true, even when already listed or previously absent. Answer existence and stated-purpose questions from metadata; read or use the Skill only when the user asks to inspect or apply its instructions. Also refresh after writes or to request the latest directory; selected Skill versions stay fixed. Report matching availability. Only fresh online results with exhaustive coverage and no failures establish that no available match was found in the searched scope; stale, offline, failed or partial results cannot establish current absence. Use search_in:content only when the user asks to search Skill content. Content mode requires a nonempty query and one configured source, performs an authorized remote Notion search, and may request foreground OAuth. Content results are always non-exhaustive and do not prove exact fixed Skill or supporting-file bytes match. Content mode has no cursor; limit is at most 50. It never adopts or changes task instructions.
tools.name: notion_list

cursor.description: Metadata only: copy next_cursor to continue the same query and metadata publication; restart after refresh. Content mode rejects all cursors.

limit.description: Maximum entries, default 20. Content search accepts at most 50 and has no pagination.

query.description: A short name or description keyword; empty lists the metadata directory. Content search requires a nonempty user-requested query.

refresh.description: Refresh metadata for the explicit source, or this accepted turn's selected Library when source is omitted. Keeps task pins; configured offline sources remain offline. Does not refresh the remote full-text index. Cannot combine with cursor.

search_in.description: Default metadata searches names and descriptions without MCP or authorization UI. Content explicitly searches remote Notion content in one configured source.

source.description: Configured source ID. Omission uses this accepted turn's selected Library for metadata and content search.

tools.description: Load task roots directly to apply their instructions; no preliminary read is needed. Requires load automatically: do not add them as independent roots unless independently requested. To introduce, summarize or inspect a Skill, use read instead. Copy a supplied ref, or pass task roots together. Use refresh:true only for a requested update; the supplied current or fixed main ref locates the same owner's latest version. Refresh roots with conflicting shared Requires together. Members remain candidates. Loading does not authorize executing a workflow. Notion consumption does not write to Notion.
tools.name: notion_use

ref.description: Supplied sr:C/sr:S or skill://<stable-skill-id>[/<main>][?library=<root-page-uuid>] refs, or exact Notion Skill page URLs for task roots. Requires are included automatically. Copy returned canonical refs; names and aliases are discovery labels.

refresh.description: Explicitly adopt current versions for only these roots after a complete successful load. Existing Requires-only nodes cannot become independent roots through refresh; explicitly use them without refresh first. Accepts the supplied sr:C/sr:S or main ref unchanged, for example {ref:[REF_A,REF_B],refresh:true} for shared roots. Failure keeps the previous selection.

tools.description: Inspect this branch's Skill graph or working_set. working_set show lists confirmed roots, Requires, visible instruction bytes and the session budget; budget explicitly sets max_bytes, null disables it; release retires only the supplied fixed roots and preserves shared Requires, Session history and Notion. Alternatively request cli_source for one exact configured Notion source's host-local CLI prefix when an authorized maintenance/source task needs it. These operations do not execute CLI commands or grant authorization. Choose only one operation.
tools.name: notion_ctl

cli_source.description: Use null for this accepted turn’s Library, or an exact enabled Notion source ID to choose another write target. Returns the verified root scope and host-local command prefix without execution.

max_bytes.description: For budget only. Complete active instruction closure in UTF-8 bytes, not tokens. Explicit null disables the budget. No automatic eviction or truncation.

refs.description: Optional fixed sr:S/sr:R references to export as canonical identity and exact version proofs for independent validation.

roots.description: For release only. Copy fixed root refs from working_set show or selected sr:S refs. Required-only nodes cannot be released directly.

working_set.description: Inspect, explicitly budget, or release this session's Notion root/Requires working set. No remote writes or historical deletion.

tools.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
tools.name: codemode
